report: This 13-year-old girl presented with three months of bilateral, migrating polyarthritis, subcutaneous nodules on extensor surfaces, and a grade 3 apical holosystolic murmur with exertional dyspnea and orthopnea, two weeks after an upper respiratory infection with high fever. Laboratory data show marked inflammation (ESR 120, CRP 2.3) and a markedly elevated ASO titer of 832, confirming antecedent group A streptococcal infection. Echocardiography demonstrates severe mitral regurgitation, mild aortic regurgitation, and pericardial effusion, documenting valvular carditis. Applying the Jones criteria, the patient has multiple major manifestations (polyarthritis, subcutaneous nodules, carditis) plus serologic evidence of preceding streptococcal infection, satisfying the diagnosis. The high ASO titer and chronic polyarthritis with nodules argue strongly against infective endocarditis, and valvular involvement with pericardial effusion is atypical for juvenile idiopathic arthritis, whose probability falls to 0.10. The frontier 'rheumatic fever with carditis' is the finest clinically actionable level, so the diagnosis and its streptococcal etiology are established.
